I tried to hit all the big things because I didn't quite get what you were getting at. It's important to note what you mean by IP, because IP has no real meaning.
<hippie> You can't own ideas maaan. </hippie>
Trademark means you can't pretend to be another company or their product. This lasts as long as you have the company. Copyright says you still don't own the idea, but you own a particular expression of that idea. These are supposed to be time limited, but thanks to Disney, are effectively forever. Patents do allow you time-limited, exclusive commercial use of a significant, new idea.

The term IP tries to put these very different things into one basket to imply it's just like owning a car. It's mostly used by lazy/bad journalists, PR, and sue-happy organizations.
